title: The reshimu and the Kav: one power to unite and to measure, from the Essence itself
overview:
Chapter 15 gives the *nimshal* of the teacher of chapter 14. The *reshimu* left in the empty place is, for the Kabbalists, the *yud* of *SaG*, *Malchus* of *tevuna*; in plain terms it is the teacher's point, a *hiyuli* that holds everything. The *Kav* drawn from it is *mamash* the infinite light, narrowed only for the receivers. The lower it goes, the more it shows the whole power, and the aim is that the student become a Rebbe himself.

The *Kav* has two opposite powers: it unites everything, and as the *kav hamida* it measures everything apart. Both are true and each depends on the other, like the king who can jail you and pardon you. Really these are not things: it is the *Aibershter*, who can be infinite, zero, or anything between. So He can also break His own plan, with more light (the class trip to NASA, the fireworks at Sinai) or less (the class that sits and does nothing, exile), and we can ask Him to change the will itself. The two powers weigh the same, and even in a kindergarten you get the whole power of the teacher.

sections.title: The reshimu: the yud of SaG, a hiyuli that holds everything
sections.summary: The *nimshal* of the teacher's point is the *reshimu* left in the empty place. In Kabbalistic terms it is the *yud* of *SaG*, *Malchus* of *tevuna*; in plain terms it is a *hiyuli* that holds everything, and it limits the light to a line only for the sake of the receivers.

phrases.he: (טו) והנמשל מכל הנזכר לעיל יובן
בבחינת רושם שנשאר בחלל ומקום פנוי הנזכר לעיל
(שהוא יו"ד דס"ג שבטהירו עילאה
phrases.en: which is the *yud* of the *SaG*; this *reshimu* is the *yud* of the *SaG* into *tehiru ila'a*

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בספר עמק המלך)
phrases.en: as it explains in *Emek HaMelech*

blocks.text: Chapter 14 gave the analogy; here is the *nimshal*: the *roshem* that remained in the *chalal*, the empty place. And the text adds in parentheses that this *reshimu* (the impression left after the *tzimtzum*) is the *yud* of *SaG* in the *tehiru ila'a*, as *Emek HaMelech* explains. What does that mean exactly?

First of all, these parentheses are really footnotes. In a book printed the way we do books now they would belong at the bottom of the page. And they are footnotes like the footnotes in the *Rambam*, not like a *Rashi*. *Rashi* explains to you what it says; a footnote in the *Rambam*, when you look down there, makes it totally more difficult, and brings in a whole bunch of extra things. These are footnotes for the Kabbalists, for the very advanced people, and to understand the book you can really totally skip this one. ("But you explained it to me," the student says, twice. So he explains.)

The basic thing is this. It is the *daled rabsi*, the big *daled*: *Malchus* of *tevuna* (understanding, as it draws an idea out). The *yud* of the *SaG* is the last *yud* of the *SaG*. *SaG* is the Name spelled with *yuds* and an *alef*, and if you add it up there are ten letters. The Names are four letters, the four levels *ABYA*; when you expand them you have ten letters. So the *yud* of the *SaG* is the last one, and it is *Malchus* of *tevuna*.

*BaN* has only nine letters; all the other spellings have ten (the student mixes them up, and they go back and forth until it is straight). And the *reshimu* is *Malchus* of *tevuna*. That is exactly what was said before about the *reshimu*: when the teacher thinks to himself of what he is going to teach, he has it all down to a point, and from this point everything will come out, all the explanations. That is *Malchus* of *tevuna*. And this is also the source of... *AB*, *SaG*, which is the source of the *shevira* (the breaking) and the source of the repair. And the *roshem* that remained is the *Malchus* of *tevuna*.

The Name *Havaya*, spelled out, is made up of four Names: *AB*, *SaG*, *MaH* and *BaN*. What happens, it says, is that they fold over: *MaH* goes into *AB*, and *BaN* goes into *SaG*. But *BaN* only has nine letters, so the *yud* from the *SaG* is left over.

Why does *BaN* have only nine letters? Because, as you learn later about the *nesira* (the sawing apart), before the *nesira* there are only nine *sefiros* of *Malchus*. *Malchus* receives from all the other *Malchuyos*: the actual building is the building of *Malchus* of *Malchus*. But the main place it receives from is the *yud* of *SaG*, *Malchus* of *tevuna*.

What it means is that the letters of *dibur* (speech) receive from the letters of *machshava* (thought). "The mother lends the clothes to the daughter." Speech really has all nine *sefiros*: in the desire to speak you already have all the *middos*. The only thing you do not have is the actual letters. The letters, the five *gevuros*, come from thought, and the letters of thought come from the *yud* of the *SaG*, from *Malchus* of *tevuna*.

The inner side of the *yud* of the *SaG* is *Malchus* of *bina*. There is the *yud* of the *SaG* as it is to itself, and the *yud* of the *SaG* as it is going to go down; that is *Malchus* of *tevuna*. It is like the *yichuda ila'a* and the *yichuda tata'a* (the higher and the lower unity): "*Havaya* is our G-d, *Havaya* is one" is the upper one, and "Blessed be the Name" the lower one, in terms of *Atzilus* and *Beriya*. But this is higher: this is the *Atzilus* of the whole, and *Adam Kadmon* is the *Beriya* of the whole. This is where the *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* really receives from: *Malchus* of *tevuna*.

The letters of the *reshimu*, which go over from before to after and are *boke'a* (break through) into the *Kav*, have to come from *tevuna*. It says that the *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* breaks through the *masach*; not the *masach*, he corrects himself: through the *tzimtzum*, through the *reshimu*. So where does it come from? The letters of *Malchus* are the letters of speech or of writing, and it says that the letters written in the Ten Commandments on the Tablets are the actual letters of the *reshimu*. But they came from *Malchus* of *tevuna*. That is where the building of *Malchus* of *Malchus* came from.

But it really does not matter. That is the Kabbalistic manner. The basic thing is what he says: the *nimshal* of all the above. He already explained the whole thing to us better than this, what it is talking about: the *roshem* which remained in the *chalal*, the empty place.

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת היולי
phrases.en: That the *reshimu* is a *hiyuli*

phrases.he: כולל כל מה שיסתעף ממנו על ידי הקו וחוט כו'
phrases.en: which includes anything which will branch out of it through the *Kav v'chut*

phrases.he: וגם שנתעלם כללות האור העצמות
עד שלא נשאר רק בחינת רשימו,
phrases.en: still there's nothing but *reshimu* left

phrases.he: עם כל זה ודאי הכל נכלל בו בקיצור
על ידי זה הצמצום דווקא
כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: like was explained before

blocks.text: The *reshimu* is a *hiyuli* which includes anything that will branch out of it through the *Kav* and the thread. And even though nothing is left but a *reshimu*, still, certainly everything is included in it in short. He is recapping here all the way back to chapter 12.

phrases.he: וגם מה שהוא מורה העדר ההתפשטות למטה,
אינו בחינת צמצום גמור
רק מצד שהוא בחינת כח ההיולי כו' כנזכר לעיל
רק להיותו כח מגביל לכללות האור הראשון, על כן בלתי מתפשט רק דרך קו,
phrases.en: Since it's the *koach hamagbil*, that's why the light in it, even when it is *misposhet*, is not *misposhet* in an infinite way like it was before, but only in a *metzumtzam* way, *derech Kav*

phrases.he: לפי אופן ההשפעה כנזכר לעיל.
phrases.en: according to the *hashpa'a*, which goes according to the *mekabel*

blocks.text: As explained in the last chapter, the *reshimu* shows *davka* an absence of spreading forth below. That is not a complete *tzimtzum*. Since it is the limiting power, the light in it, even when it spreads forth, does not spread in an infinite way as it did before, but only in a contracted way, by way of a line, according to the manner of the giving. And the giving goes according to the *mekabel* (the receiver).

sections.title: The Kav is the infinite light itself, narrowed only for the receivers
sections.summary: The *Kav* has in it the power of the first light, *mamash* as the *Ein Sof*; it comes as a line only because of the receivers. Like the *ish tevuna* who brings it down to the sheep, the lower it goes, the more it shows the whole power, and the aim is that the student become a Rebbe himself.

phrases.he: אמנם יובן מהנזכר לעיל
דקו זה יש בו מכח האור הראשון שלפני הצמצום
בבחינת אין סוף ממש,
רק שבא דרך קו, לפי אופן המקבלים כו'
phrases.en: the only reason it comes because of *Kav* is because of the *mekablim davka*, not because of the *mashpia*

blocks.text: this *Kav* has in it of the power of the first light before the *tzimtzum*, *mamash* as the *Ein Sof*. First of all, the *reshimu* itself has the entire *Ein Sof* in it. And not only the *reshimu*: the *Kav*, as it expands, can be expanded all the way back to the original light.

blocks.title: The Rogatchover talking to his equal
blocks.text: If the teacher is talking to somebody on his own level, *mamash*, he can tell him exactly. If the Rogatchover is talking to another guy like that, and not to little students, then it is *mamash* as the *Ein Sof*, even in the *Kav*. That the *Kav* has a measurement according to the *mekablim* depends on who the *mekabel* is. If he is somebody like himself, he can expand it, and *mamash* the whole *Or Ein Sof* is in there. only that it comes by way of a line, according to the manner of the receivers: the only reason it comes as a *Kav* is *davka* the *mekablim*, not the *mashpia* (the giver).

phrases.he: ובזה יובן מה שכתוב באורך נראה אור
בחינת הארה דהארה הנקרא אור של תולדה
phrases.en: a secondary light, which is called *haara d'haara*, *or shel tolda*

phrases.he: שאחר הצמצום בוקע האור דרך קו בעלמא כו',
phrases.en: it only breaks through in a very *metzumtzam* way, just like a little line of light

phrases.he: אבל הוא בא מאורך העצמי
להיות שברשימו הרי נכלל הכל וממנו נמשך הקו
phrases.en: it's the whole thing of the *reshimu* that goes into the *Kav*, and the *reshimu* has the whole thing of the whole *Ein Sof*

phrases.he: בבחינת היולי לכללות השפע
להיות בבחינת מעלה ומטה על כל פנים,
כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים

blocks.text: "In Your light we see light": this explanation for the *mekabel* really comes from the actual light of the *mashpia*. Even though it is a secondary light, which is called *haara d'haara*, a glow of a glow, and called a light of offspring, still it really comes from the original light.

after the *tzimtzum* the light breaks through only by way of a mere line: it breaks through in a very contracted way, just like a little line of light. but it comes from Your essential light. The whole *reshimu* goes into the *Kav*, and the *reshimu* has the whole *Ein Sof*.

blocks.question: The *tevuna* explains according to the receiver; so is the light of the *Kav* not according to the receiver after all?
blocks.text:
He first ties "but it comes from Your essential light" to the *tevuna*: that's from the *tevuna*. Then the word is settled: the student reads *me'erech*, and it is not *erech*, it is "Your light", the light of "In Your light we see light". Then he presses: this goes back to what was said before, that the *tevuna* of the *Aibershter* (the One Above) is according to the *mekabel*.

The *tevuna* itself is not. The *tevuna* itself is the *Aibershter*'s *tevuna*, and everything is in there. Even though it is a *tevuna*, and now He is going to put it into an explanation according to the *mekabel*, the *tevuna* itself is the *Aibershter*'s. And not only the flow itself: even the later explanation, which is only according to the measure of the *mekabel*, comes *mamash* from the actual knowledge of the *mashpia*.

Not only that. As was said of the three thousand analogies of Shlomo: the lower down it goes, the higher up it shows. That he can bring it lower down shows, especially in the *tevuna*, that there is more of the *etzem* (the essence) there.

blocks.title: The long nun in the Hebrew notebook
blocks.text: That is why the *tevuna* is a long *nun*. When they teach little kids how to write Hebrew, did you ever see the Hebrew notebooks? They are not like the English ones. The English one is just a bunch of lines. In the Hebrew ones each line has a space on top and on the bottom: the *lamed* goes up past the line, and the *nun* goes down past the line. It goes past its own place into the next level.

That is the whole thing of *tevuna*. As was said, the *ish tevuna* (the man of *tevuna*) can *davka* bring it down to the sheep: not to his own level but to a lower level. And that shows even more what a great *ish tevuna* he is than the actual *bina* itself. That is what makes him an *ish tevuna*. The lower down it goes, the higher up he is.

So in terms of the *Kav*: that the *Kav* can go down shows that it is really the whole *koach* (power) of the *Or Ein Sof*. The same with the explanation. Even though the explanation is a lesser thing than the way he understands it himself, it is an actual light that comes from his own inner light. So the light that comes into the *Kav* is *mamash* the power of the original light. It does not need to be contracted; it can stop being contracted and become the whole original light.

blocks.title: The student will be a Rebbe himself
blocks.text: Not only that: it is not really a *tzimtzum*. That is the whole *kavana* (intention). The intention in the *Kav* is not to bring a contracted light down. In the analogy of the Rebbe with the student, the intention is not just to explain a little tiny explanation to the student. The intention is that by the end of all the explanations he gets the whole thing. And not just that he gets the whole thing and finally understands the same as the Rebbe: he will be a Rebbe himself, just like the Rebbe. So it is really going to pass over the whole *Atzmus* (the Essence), which means that the whole *etzem* is in there. And all this so that there is at least an above and a below, as it says in *Etz Chaim*.

sections.title: Two opposites in the Kav: it unites everything, and it measures everything
sections.summary: The *Kav* includes the left in the right and makes all the unifications, down to a light in a vessel not its own; and it is the *kav hamida*, which measures every light and vessel apart. The power to divide is the same power as the power to connect.

phrases.he: ומזה הטעם יובן תירוץ על
ב' ענינים הפכים שנמצא בקו זה
phrases.en: the two opposites which is in the *Kav*

phrases.he: הא' אשר בכחו דוקא לאכללא שמאלא בימינא כו'
שהוא בחינת ההתכללות והיחודים
של כל האורות המסתעפים מכתר דאדם קדמון עד מלכות דאצילות
עד שעל ידו דוקא יוחלף האור בכלי שאינו שלו,
כמו אור החסד בכלי הגבורה כו'
כמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות
phrases.en: This will be explained later, I think it's chapter 21 or 22 or something like that

phrases.he: בענין וא''ו דוהנורא כו'

blocks.text: There are two opposite things that are found in this *Kav*. The first: that *davka* it has the power "to include the left in the right", the *hiskalelus* and *yichudim* of all the lights from *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon* to *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, so that *davka* through it a light is exchanged into a vessel that is not its own. *Davka* the *Kav* is the power of all the unifications. This will be explained later, he thinks in chapter 21 or 22 or something like that.

Because it is from the *Atzmus*, that is why there is a *hiskalelus*: in the *Atzmus* it is all one. That is why the *Kav* can really include everything together. It really has the power of the essence of the *Or Ein Sof*, where these things are totally non-differentiated.

on the *vav* of "and the awesome": "the great, the mighty and the awesome" that we say of the *Aibershter*. "The great", *chesed*, is the *Or Ein Sof*; "the mighty" is the *tzimtzum*; and "and the awesome" is the *Kav*. The *vav* of *v'hanora* is the *Kav*.

phrases.he: והב' מה שנקרא בשם קו המדה דוקא,
למדוד כל אורות וכלים כו'
וכנזכר לעיל בענין הקו שנקרא אמת הבנין כו'
שזהו היפוך ההתכללות לכאורה.
phrases.en: that's the opposite

blocks.text: And the second: that it is called by the name *kav hamida*. What does it mean, that it measures? Measuring means that each one is different. to measure all lights and vessels is what makes this one *chachma* and this one *bina*: two different things, by measuring what the measurement of each thing is. And it is *haynu hach*, one and the same: the power to divide is the power to connect. It is *mamash* the same power, and it includes both powers in it.

which is, seemingly, the opposite of the *hiskalelus*. To measure means this one is this and this one is that: the right and the left and the middle. As it says, "one long, one short and one in between". It measures the long one and the short one, the right and the left.

sections.title: Both are true, and each depends on the other: the power of the Essence and the power of the reshimu
sections.summary: The one who can keep you out is the one who can let you in. From the Essence in the *Kav* comes the power to unite; from the *reshimu* in it comes the power to measure, and the inner *MaH*, the *kav hamida*, already holds every *midda* the teacher will ever show. But really these are not things: it is the *Aibershter* Himself, who can be in infinite mode, in zero mode, or anywhere in between.

phrases.he: אך הענין הוא דשניהם אמת
phrases.en: Really, they're both true. It has both powers.

phrases.he: ואדרבה הא בהא תליא
phrases.en: not only that, just the opposite: the one is connected to the other

blocks.text: But the point is that both are true: it has both powers. And not only that, just the opposite: the one depends on the other. Because he has the power to separate, he has the power to connect; and because he has the power to connect, he has the power to separate.

blocks.title: The guard at the border and in the prison
blocks.text: On the border, the guy who has the power to keep you out is the same guy who has the power to let you through. That is the guy, and it is really the power of the king. The same in a prison: the one who has the power to put you in there is the one who has the power to take you out. So you go to the guard and say, "Let me out. Hey, you're the guard, let me out." He says, "I don't have the power to let you out. If you want to be let out, you got to go back to whoever put you in here, the judge." He's got the power.

blocks.title: The judge only follows the law
blocks.text: And really even the judge does not have the power, because the judge can only go by the law. You go to the judge, and he says, "Well, I can't let you out." "What do you mean? You put me in here!" "Really, I didn't put you in here. I just do my job, the same as the guard. I had to put you in there because you broke the law, and the law tells me that whoever breaks the law has to go in for a certain amount of time. That's what I did; I just followed the law."

blocks.title: Only the king can pardon
blocks.text: "So you have to go to the king. He made the law to put you in, so he can pardon you, even against the law." ("Huh?" Yes: a pardon means against the law. He made the law in the first place, so he can pardon you.) The judge says, "I can't pardon you. I can only go according to the law. I don't really have the power to put you in there; I didn't put you in there, the law put you in there. I'm just the guy who decides according to the law." If you want, you have to go to the originator of the law. The one who puts you in there is the one who can take you out. It is *mamash* the same power: the one who can divide is the one who can connect. the one depends on the other.

phrases.he: משום דשרש זה הקו
מכח הראשון דעצמיות אור אין סוף שלפני הצמצום הוא בא
כנזכר לעיל בענין באורך דוקא נראה אור דקו זה
ובכח האור העצמות דאין סוף
phrases.en: In the power of the *Ein Sof*

phrases.he: ודאי יש לעשות בחינת התכללות ויחודים של כל ההפכים בכל ההשתלשלות
phrases.en: there's certainly a power to make all the *yichudim* in all the *hishtalshelus*

phrases.he: מראש דאדם קדמון כו' עד מלכות דאצילות
וכמאמר אנת הוא דמייחד לון ומקשר לון כו',
phrases.en: you're the one that unifies and ties them together

phrases.he: אנת הוא מלגאו ומלבר כו'
phrases.en: you're from the inside and you're from the outside

blocks.text: Because the root of this *Kav* comes from the first power of the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*, as was said about "the way it goes out shines for him". In the power of the *Ein Sof* there is certainly a power to make all the *yichudim* in the whole chain of descent, because in the *Or Ein Sof* they are all one. "You are the one who unifies them and ties them together"; "You are within and without": You are from the inside and You are from the outside.

phrases.he: וכן ענין שם מ''ה מלגאו
phrases.en: the thing of the *Shem MaH* on the inside

phrases.he: דאיהו אורח כל האצילות כו'
phrases.en: which is the way of the whole *Atzilus*

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא

blocks.text: the inner Name *MaH*, which is the path of all of *Atzilus*. What does that mean? The Name *MaH* is basically the line. Of the four, *AB*, *SaG*, *MaH* and *BaN*, *MaH* is the *vav*: in general *Zeir Anpin* and the *middos* (attributes) coming down. And *middos* means the *kav hamida*, that it measures it. That is the measurement.

It comes from the *reshimu*, which is the *SaG*, and then the line comes down, the Name *MaH*, the path of all of *Atzilus*. Not a length: *orach* is a path, a pathway, the pathway of the entire *Atzilus*. The light of the line comes down to the end of *Atzilus*. That is the inner *MaH*. The outer *MaH* is another, lower *MaH*; the inner *MaH* is this line.

"I am not exactly sure exactly how it works," but the basic thing is that the *yud* at the head of the *vav* is not the upper *yud*. It is the *yud* at the end of the *hei*, the end of the *SaG*. From *Malchus* of *tevuna* come the *middos*. You will learn later that even though they come from *daas*, *Abba* and *Ima*, *chachma* and *bina*, are called the upper *Abba* and *Ima*, and *tevuna* is called *Ima tata'a* (the lower mother), because the actual coming out of the *middos* comes *davka* from *tevuna*, not from *bina*; and it comes out from *Malchus* of *tevuna*.

So *kav hamida*: a *midda* and *middos* mean the same thing. *Middos* does not actually mean emotions. *Middos* really means measurements, and the measurements are the long, the short and the medium. That is the three *middos*. Really there are three *middos*, not seven. Seven means the three *middos*, then the three reactions of the *middos*, and then *Malchus*, the extension of the *middos* to the outside. So there is *Chagas*, then *Nehi*; the essence of the *middos* is *Chagas*. That is why you learn later of the big *vav* and the little *vav*.

And there they call it Yaakov and Yosef. Yaakov is called Yaakov and Yisroel, and then there is Yosef. *Zeir Anpin* is sometimes called Yaakov and sometimes Yosef: as *Chagas* it is called Yaakov, and as *Nehi* it is called Yosef. Yosef is "the righteous one, the foundation of the world", and Yaakov is the attribute of truth, *tiferes*. Sometimes it is also called Noach, when it is the outside of it: the outside of *Nehi* is called Noach.

But the basic thing is the *midda*: that is why they are called *middos*. A *midda* is a measurement, and that is what a characteristic means. They are called emotions; they really should all be called characteristics. The emotion comes out of the characteristic. "What are his *middos*" does not mean what emotion he is having now; it means what his characteristic is. A man of the *midda* of *gevura*, a *kaasan* (an angry man), does not mean that right now he is angry. It means he has a characteristic that he tends to get angry. And a *chasdan* does not mean that right now he is doing a kindness; it means he has the characteristic of being a kind guy.

The next side opens in the middle of the same point. The *Kav* is the inner *MaH*, the *kav hamida*, the line that measures. The outer *MaH* is the *middos* of *Atzilus*. And the path of all of *Atzilus* means that the whole measurement that will later be in *Atzilus*, in its *MaH*, the outer *MaH*, comes from the inner *MaH*: it is already included in the inner *MaH* of the *Kav*.

blocks.title: Every midda the teacher will show is already there
blocks.text: Take this in terms of the analogy of the *hiyuli* for measurement in the teacher. All the characteristics he will display in the actual day-to-day teaching, the seven days of the week, the "days of the world", are already included in this *kav hamida*. The whole way he is going to act is already there. And he will act a different way for different classes.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 013 opens in the middle of class 012's explanation of line 28 and stays with it until it finishes reading the line at w1519.

blocks.title: A boys' class and a girls' class
blocks.text: He measures it: if you give him a boys' class or a girls' class, let's say. In a boys' class you have to have a little bit more discipline. Like "speak to the children of Israel" and "say": the *Aibershter* told Moshe that to the men you have to talk tough, and to the ladies you have to talk in a nice way.

sensitivity.reason: A generalisation about how boys and girls, men and women, must be spoken to.
sensitivity.publishable: He measures it: a teacher speaks to each class in the way that class needs. As the *Aibershter* told Moshe to speak one way and to say another, one group needs firmer words and another gentler ones.

blocks.outOfPlace: Class 013 opens in the middle of class 012's explanation of line 28 and stays with it until it finishes reading the line at w1519.

blocks.title: The geniuses and the ghetto school
blocks.text: Or tell the man, "We're going to put you in a class with the top students in the country, special geniuses, totally motivated," or else, "We're going to put you in the worst ghetto school there is." He is going to relate to them differently. They come there with guns; their little five-year-old kids are already carrying guns. So obviously he will have to show different *middos*. But it is all included in the inner *MaH*, all already there in the *kav hamida*, and this is what is going to measure, according to the different *mekablim*, what *middos* will be shown, what kind of a character he will put forth.

sensitivity.reason: Caricatures children of a poor urban school as five-year-olds carrying guns.
sensitivity.publishable: Or tell the man, "We're going to put you in a class with the top students in the country, special geniuses, totally motivated," or else, "We're going to put you in the hardest school there is." He is going to relate to them differently, and obviously he will have to show different *middos*. But it is all included in the inner *MaH*, all already there in the *kav hamida*, and this is what is going to measure, according to the different *mekablim*, what *middos* will be shown, what kind of a character he will put forth.

blocks.outOfPlace: Class 013 opens in the middle of class 012's explanation of line 28 and stays with it until it finishes reading the line at w1519.

blocks.text: It is able to relate to each specific *mekabel* *davka* because of the power of the *Atzmus*. Really it is from two things. One is the power of the *Atzmus*. The other is that the *midda* is *davka* from the power of the *tzimtzum* and *reshimu*, which can separate out a different thing for different people: the opposite of its including everything. But it includes both, and that is the Name *MaH*: in general *MaH* is *Zeir Anpin*, or *tiferes*, which includes the two sides.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 013 opens in the middle of class 012's explanation of line 28 and stays with it until it finishes reading the line at w1519.

blocks.text: Up there it is also like that: "the great, the mighty and the awesome". "And the awesome" means that the *Kav* is an equal force. It seems not to be the same: first the *Or Ein Sof*, the real big force; then after the *tzimtzum* nothing is left but a *reshimu*, which is somehow a lesser thing; and then the *Kav* is only what comes out, and the *reshimu* is its *hiyuli*. So the *Kav* is *mamash* a nothing, because it comes out in a limited way: nothing compared to the original infinite light. What he is saying here is that it is not like that.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 013 opens in the middle of class 012's explanation of line 28 and stays with it until it finishes reading the line at w1519.

blocks.text: "The great, the mighty and the awesome" are right, left and middle, three of the same level. Not only that: Yaakov is the choicest of the Avos because he includes both of them. It is *davka* Yaakov who includes, which means that the *Kav* has both powers in it. And it is the middle bar, the one that runs through from end to end.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 013 opens in the middle of class 012's explanation of line 28 and stays with it until it finishes reading the line at w1519.

blocks.title: Writing lines, or teaching him everything
blocks.text: The *Kav* can contract all the way down to the level of the *reshimu* if he needs to: he will not teach the class anything at all, he will make them all write lines or sit in the corner, or he can even put a kid outside the class, which means he is not teaching him at all. A total *tzimtzum*. And if he wants, if he has an equal to himself, he can really teach him the whole entire thing, not just a contracted line. The *Kav* can actually expand to the whole original thing; it can be the whole infinite light. That is "and the awesome": the *Kav* is the *tiferes* of the *Or Ein Sof*, what balances the other two.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 013 opens in the middle of class 012's explanation of line 28 and stays with it until it finishes reading the line at w1519.

blocks.text: Not only that: it is not just the *tiferes* of the *Or Ein Sof*, it is the *tiferes* of the *Maor* (the source of the light). The *Or Ein Sof* is the *chesed* of a higher thing. In this system the *Or Ein Sof* is what he is calling "the great", the *tzimtzum* and the *reshimu* "the mighty", and the *Kav* "and the awesome". And who is this? "The G-d": the *Aibershter* Himself.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 013 opens in the middle of class 012's explanation of line 28 and stays with it until it finishes reading the line at w1519.

blocks.text: "The great, the mighty and the awesome" means that the line is not really the line, not the *kav hamida*: it is the teacher himself. It is not that there is an actual *kav hamida* that you take. The original thing is the teacher who knows the original thing, and he contracts the whole thing. When we say "the *tzimtzum* and the *reshimu*", that just means a power: it is just a description of something the teacher himself did.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 013 opens in the middle of class 012's explanation of line 28 and stays with it until it finishes reading the line at w1519.

blocks.title: The cat's power of movement
blocks.text: There is no such thing as "the power of movement". A cat can run because he has the body of a cat. Destroy the body of the cat, and he can't run. There is no power of movement apart from his body; it is not a separate thing. "Well, we killed the cat, but here's his power of movement." There ain't no power of movement. Power of movement really means that he can move. Without the cat there is no power of movement.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 013 opens in the middle of class 012's explanation of line 28 and stays with it until it finishes reading the line at w1519.

blocks.text: By the way, this is also what was talked about before. It is a very big mistake people make, separating these things into things: to think that the *reshimu* is a thing and the *Kav* is a thing, there's this thing and there's that thing. It does not work like that; that is not what it means. That is the whole thing he was talking about in chapter 4: when you learn it properly, the particulars do not take away from the whole. We are not really talking about the *Kav* over here at all. We are not talking about *Atzilus*, or the *Or Ein Sof*, or the *yud* of *SaG*. We are talking about the *Aibershter*. That's what we're talking about: we are talking about the *Aibershter*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 013 opens in the middle of class 012's explanation of line 28 and stays with it until it finishes reading the line at w1519.

blocks.text: When we talk about the *Kav*, we are saying that the *Aibershter* can measure the *mekabel*. That is a thing the *Aibershter* can do. When we talk about the *Or Ein Sof*, it is that the *Aibershter* can be in infinite mode. When we talk about the *tzimtzum* and the *reshimu*, it is that the *Aibershter* can be in zero mode. And the *Kav* means that the *Aibershter* can be in any mode He wants in between. He can do anything He wants: if He wants He can be infinite, if He wants He can be totally finite, and if He wants He can be anywhere in the middle.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 013 opens in the middle of class 012's explanation of line 28 and stays with it until it finishes reading the line at w1519.

blocks.text: ("We're on the bottom line," of the page.) It is all from the glow of the light of the Essence of the *Ein Sof* in this *Kav*, which goes and is drawn all the way down into *Malchus*, the end of all levels: he is talking about *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, and it could also be talking about *Malchus* of *Asiya*.

And that is the very thing that gives it the power to measure: that it can spread downwards all the way to the end of all levels is the same thing that gives it the power to measure for every light and vessel and for every unification of *mashpia* and *mekabel*, how much *mayin duchrin* and *mayin nukvin* there will be: the influence from above and the influence from below. In terms of the different classes, he measures it all.

from the side of the *reshimu*, which limits: that is the power of limitation. And both of these powers are included in the *Kav*, as He estimated in the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*: these different ways of the contractions were already estimated before the actual *tzimtzum*. As was said of reaching for the vodka bottle, or of the cat jumping.

נקרא בחינת היולי ליכלל ולחבר את הכל כו',

blocks.text: from the side of the Essence of the light in the *Kav*, it is called a *hiyuli* to include and to join everything: it is the *hiyuli* for all the unifications. and from the side of the limiting power of the *reshimu* in it, it can make all the limits and give a measure and size to everything, according to the original *shiur* in the *glif glifu* (He engraved an engraving), which was included in the *reshimu*.

as in the analogy of a craftsman who makes an outline: he makes a blueprint, so that everything comes out exact, that it should not turn right or left from the original plan. And yet he does not have to rethink the whole plan anymore; it is all written down.

sections.title: More than the measure, or less: changes come from the Essence itself
sections.summary: When a light comes that is beyond the *kav hamida*, or when the light is held back, the plan is broken, and only the teacher who made the plan can break it: the trip to NASA, the class that sits and does nothing, the giving of the Torah with all the fireworks, exile. That is why we can ask "from before You" to change the will that made the plan itself.

phrases.he: ואף על פי שאם לפעמים יהיה תוספת אור בנאצלים,
יתר מכפי מאמר קו המדה כו',
phrases.en: different from the *kav hamida*

phrases.he: היינו מכח האור העצמות דוקא
שלפעמים יאיר כך ולפעמים יאיר כך

blocks.text: at times there will be an addition of light in the emanated beings, more than the word of the *kav hamida*, different from the *kav hamida*: that is *davka* from the power of the light of the Essence, that sometimes shines this way and sometimes that way. What does that mean? That sometimes it does not go according to the *kav hamida*. So what is the *kav hamida*?

blocks.title: The class trip to NASA
blocks.text: According to the *kav hamida*, the teacher made up a class plan: on Monday we learn chapter 1, on Tuesday chapter 2, on Wednesday chapter 3. But let's say it is a science class, and on Tuesday, when they are supposed to learn chapter 3, he says to the class, "Today, instead of learning chapter 3, I'm going to take you to NASA." And at NASA they are going to see something way beyond the *kav hamida* plan of what they were supposed to learn, something with no relation at all to their level, because they don't understand what is going on over there. Or he takes them to the museum of science. So this is not according to the plan. What happened to the *kav hamida*? "Well, the teacher can do anything he wants."

blocks.title: Then why break the plan?
blocks.text: "But wait a minute, there was a plan. So why did he break the *kav hamida*?" Because when the kids go and see NASA they will see something not according to the measure of what they can understand, way beyond their capacity, and this will give them a taste for it, so that they will want to become scientists. And really that is part of the plan. So it seems to be part of the *kav hamida*, if it is part of the plan? No, it is not part of the *kav hamida*. The *kav hamida* is according to their measure, and this is not according to their measure at all.

Then let's go the other way, he says, let's go to the side of *gevura*. But first, what the student just said is something like a miracle (the student says so, and he agrees). A miracle does not go according to the place and its measure, like the splitting of the Sea. It is not according to what is supposed to happen, not according to the plan of creation. It goes outside of nature.

blocks.title: Sit there and shut up
blocks.text: Well, that is the positive side. What about the negative? The negative side is: today they were bad, and we were supposed to do chapter four, and instead everybody is just going to sit there and do nothing. You just have to sit there and shut up. So what is going on? You're not teaching them nothing. This was not the plan; it is a breaking of the plan. He gave out the curriculum at the beginning: on Wednesday we were supposed to study chapter four. It says it right there; it is in the blueprint. On Tuesday we went to NASA instead, and on Wednesday we are doing nothing, or writing lines, which is not productive according to the plan of learning. So what is going on? "Because that's their punishment." And the punishment is part of getting them to behave properly so that they will study good. Who is doing this? The teacher. The teacher made the plan, and the teacher can break the plan.

He does not have to go according to the plan. He can put a light into the plan that is way too big for what was supposed to be there: an addition of light … more than the word of the *kav hamida*, that is *davka* from the power of the light of the Essence, that sometimes shines this way and sometimes that way.

blocks.text: every renewal of light in *ABYA* (*Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*) is all *davka* from the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*, because the *Aibershter* Himself is doing it. sometimes with more and sometimes with less: sometimes it is less than what you are supposed to get. like the change from the time of the Temple to the time of exile: how things are now is not really according to plan.

According to plan, a person is supposed to be able to get a Jewish education. People are actually not able to get a Jewish education even if they wanted to; it is not available to them. What's going on? "I mean, You want people to be religious, so why are You making a *golus* (exile) like this?"

blocks.title: "I want them to suffer"
blocks.text: It is the same kind of thing. If you want to teach these kids, why are you making them sit there the whole day doing nothing, just suffering? "That's what I want. I want them to suffer, because they were bad boys. I want them to suffer, so that next time they won't do it no more." But it is not really according to the *kav hamida*. According to the *kav hamida*, if everybody had cooperated properly, it did not have to be like this; it could have gone according to plan. Because they did not, you have to make an extreme thing to one side. And sometimes you make an extreme thing to one side in order to give them extra.

blocks.title: Why the fireworks at Sinai?
blocks.text: Like at the giving of the Torah: you didn't have to have all that hullabaloo. It could have been a quiet thing. Moshe could have gone off somewhere; it did not have to be in front of two million people. It could have been like what most of the religions claim, that some guy went to the desert and he got this thing.

sensitivity.reason: Dismisses the founding claims of most other religions as "some guy went to the desert and he got this thing".
sensitivity.publishable: Like at the giving of the Torah: you didn't have to have all that hullabaloo. It could have been a quiet thing. Moshe could have gone off somewhere by himself; it did not have to be in front of two million people.

blocks.title: Why the fireworks at Sinai?
blocks.text: As a matter of fact, why didn't He just give it to him at the burning bush? Moshe would have gone to Egypt with a *Chumash* and a *Talmud* in his hand, the whole bit, and said, "Yeah, I talked to the *Aibershter* in the desert." (He did talk to the *Aibershter* on Mount Sinai, by the way, and He told him, "You're going to come back here with all the other people, and then I'm going to give you the Torah.") And even when He gave the Torah, why did it have to be with all that noise, all the fireworks? Because He wanted to impress them, like when you take the kids to NASA. (The student adds: and the whole going out of Egypt, and everything up till then.)

blocks.title: Why the fireworks at Sinai?
blocks.text: But it is not just that. The giving of the Torah was not from the *kav hamida*, and neither was the splitting of the Sea. The whole world was shaking. The Sea did not have to be like that either: He could have just killed the Egyptians, they could have dropped dead of a heart attack, or a fire could have burned down all the pyramids. One of the things it says is that it was *davka* because He wanted to do it with water. But He could have done it in another, nice way. And especially at the giving of the Torah, the whole world was shaking, with angels flying around. What's going on here? It is not the natural order of things. *Kav hamida* means that it goes naturally according to the measurements: this is what was supposed to happen, and that is what happens. So why all of that? As He said to Moshe, "so that they should believe in you". It is done to impress them, and when you impress them like that, they will keep the Torah properly. and the like: in the time of exile as well.

phrases.he: ודרך כלל הרי אנו אומרים יהי רצון מלפניך
מלפני עצמותך ממש,
שלמעלה מי׳ ספירות העצמיים גם כן
לשנות הרצון הפשוט שכבר נמשך בעצמות האור דאין סוף
phrases.en: We want you to change the actual *ratzon*, the *ratzon* that made the *glif glifu*. We want you to change the whole plan.

phrases.he: לבא בשיעור ששיער בעצמו עד סיום הקו,
באופן אחר,
כמו מדין לחסד וכהאי גוונא

blocks.text: "May it be the will from before You": from before Your Essence, *mamash*. We are telling Him: we want You to change the actual *ratzon* (will), the *ratzon* that made the *glif glifu*. We want You to change the whole plan, as from *din* to *chesed*.

sections.title: "I have not changed": not His attributes but You
sections.summary: To ask for a new will is to ask for a change all the way back, through *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon*, in the measure itself. That is possible because the Essence is "not of these attributes at all": "You are the one who unifies them" means You, and the power of limit in the *kav hamida* also comes from the Essence.

phrases.he: וכנזכר לעיל (בסוף אות הט') בענין אני יהו״ה לא שניתי
בין רצון של חסד לדין באור הראשון שלפני הצמצום
מטעם הנזכר לעיל
(באות יו''ד) בענין חפץ חסד
שבעצמות ההיולי שנכלל בעצמות כו'
שיש בו ג' מדריגות עד שבא בדבר פרט כו'
(כמבואר באריכות באות י''א)

blocks.text: "I, *Havaya*, have not changed": between a will of *chesed* and [a will of] *din* in the first light before the *tzimtzum*: that it is really only the *tzimtzum* that changes. And this is the *chafetz chesed* which has three levels until it comes into a particular thing. What we ask is that He change all the way to the beginning, to *Yachid*, so that as it goes through *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon*, and finally to the *glif glifu*, the *Malchus* of *Kadmon* and the *shiur*, the *shiur* should be different. And so what goes into the *reshimu* will be different, and therefore what goes into the *Kav* will be different.

That is what I am asking: "and He regretted", *mamash*, a change of the whole original *ratzon*. By the way, he thinks the reference is supposed to be the end of section 8. (He reads it as section 5, and that section does not talk about "I, *Havaya*, have not changed"; the matter of "I have not changed" is really in 8 and 9. "Could be," the student says.)

phrases.he: וכשאמרו אליו ולא למדותיו,
מדבר גם במדותיו העצמיים שבאור העצמות
מפני שהעצמות דאור אין סוף, לאו מכל אלין מדות כלל כו' ודי למבין.

blocks.text: "to Him and not to His attributes" speaks even of His essential attributes: even higher than the essential *middos* of the *Or Ein Sof*. because the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* is "not of these attributes at all", which means He can change all the *middos*.

phrases.he: וזהו
phrases.en: this is what it means

phrases.he: אנת הוא דמיחד לון כו',
אנת דוקא,
phrases.en: that means *davka* You

phrases.he: שזהו אנת הוא חד ולא בחושבן י׳ ספירות כו'

blocks.text: "You", *davka*: *davka* You. They are not really different things, and the only reason you see them as different things is that you are forgetting about the You. When it is fierce, it is really the *Aibershter* who is there. You are not really dealing with the *midas hadin* (the attribute of judgement); you are really dealing with the *Aibershter*.

phrases.he: וכן מעצמות אור אין סוף דוקא בא כח הגבול והמדה
phrases.en: It's really coming from the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*

phrases.he: אשר בבחינת רשימו שבקו
שמחמת זה נקרא קו המדה
והא בהא תליה דוקא

blocks.text: the power of limit and measure that is in the *reshimu* in the *Kav*, for which it is called the *kav hamida*, is really coming from the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*. and the one *davka* depends on the other means that it is the *Aibershter* Himself who is doing it.

sections.title: Two powers of equal weight, from the Essence as it is in itself
sections.summary: In the Essence there is a power to rise higher without end and a power to spread down without end, and seen from the receiver's side they swap places, like the seal in the wax. In the *Kav* the two are equal, and every more and less, weekday and Shabbos, Temple and exile, is one power divided in two. Even in a kindergarten you get the whole power of the teacher.

phrases.he: (וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין כללות חסד וגבורה שבעצמות אור אין סוף
שהוא בחינת כח הגבול להגביל ולהעלים בעצמותו
בעילוי אחר עילוי עד אין קץ ושיעור
והיינו אור אין סוף למעלה עד אין קץ כו',
ובחינת התפשטות האור למטה מטה עד אין תכלית
שעל ידי הקו שנמשך מן הרשימו כו'

blocks.text: the power of limit, to limit and to hide in His Essence, rising higher and higher without end or measure; that is, the *Or Ein Sof* above, without end. Now he is calling it backwards. Now he says *gevura* is the light going up and up, the *Or Ein Sof*, and *chesed* is the spreading forth of the light down and down: the *tzimtzum* and *reshimu* in the *Kav* are *davka* the *chesed*. That is backwards from what was said before.

That is the general rule of the *mashpia* and the *mekabel*: when they face each other, the right of the *mashpia* becomes the left of the *mekabel*, and vice versa. In terms of the *mashpia*, the *tzimtzum* is the *gevura*. In terms of the *mekabel*, "higher and higher without end" means we do not get it, so the *Or Ein Sof* is by us a *gevura*, and the *tzimtzum* and the *reshimu* are the *chesed*. What is by Him the left side, the *tzimtzum*, is by us the right side.

blocks.title: The seal in the wax
blocks.text: That is what it means by a revelation of a revelation, what he says later on: it is like the impression of the seal in the wax. Take a seal and put it in the wax, and it is flipped around. That is the *or shel tolda*. which is through the *Kav* drawn from the *reshimu*.

phrases.he: וב' קוין שקולין המה בבחינת אין סוף
phrases.en: these are two exact powers, and they're both infinite

phrases.he: על כן גם בירידת האור דאין סוף בקו זה,
phrases.en: so in the *Kav*, also it's like that

phrases.he: שקולין ב' כחות הללו לצמצם ולהגביל או לחבר ולייחד
phrases.en: It has exactly the two powers, to expand or to contract; *tzimtzum* and *harchava* together are equal

blocks.text: the two lines are of equal weight, as *Ein Sof*: these are two exact powers, and they are both infinite. therefore also in the descent of the light of the *Ein Sof* in this *Kav*, the power of the light and the power of the *reshimu* are equal. The *reshimu* has the power to limit the entire light, and the light has the power to blot out the whole *reshimu*, to fill out the whole *chalal*.

The next tape reads the lines again: in the *Kav* it is also like that. these two powers are of equal weight: it has exactly the two powers, to expand or to contract, contraction and expansion together, and they are equal.

phrases.he: וכן ענין שינויי האור וההמשכה,
אם בתוספת או בגרעון,
phrases.en: whether the power to increase the light or the power to decrease the light

phrases.he: כמו מזמן לזמן, כמו מחול לשבת ויום טוב,
וכן מזמן בית המקדש לזמן הגלות,
הכל בכח א' שקול,
phrases.en: it's really one power

phrases.he: שנחלק לב' קוין חסד וגבורה
phrases.en: that is divided into two powers

phrases.he: הבא מכח ואור הראשון דעצמות אין סוף
כמו שהוא בעצמו
phrases.en: how He is in Himself

phrases.he: בבחינת חסד וגבורה כו' ודי למבין)
phrases.en: that the light and the *reshimu* are the *chesed* and *gevura* of the *Atzmus Ein Sof*

blocks.text: the changes of the light and of its drawing down, whether more or less: the power to increase the light or the power to decrease the light, from weekday to Shabbos and festival, from the time of the Temple to the time of exile. it is all one power, of equal weight, which is divided into two lines, *chesed* and *gevura*. It comes from the Essence of the *Ein Sof*; not the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*, he stresses, the *Atzmus Ein Sof*, as it is in itself. The light and the *reshimu* are the *chesed* and *gevura* of the *Atzmus Ein Sof*, and the line is the *tiferes*; and you can say it one way or the other, which one is the *chesed* and which the *gevura*.

phrases.he: והיינו כמבואר למעלה (באות הי''ד) דקו לגבי שטח הוא היולי
phrases.en: a line is a *hiyuli* to a *shetach*

phrases.he: כולל על דרך אותו האור וכח העצמי שבעצמות של המשפיע,
רק שבעצמות הוא בהרחבת הערך ביותר,
phrases.en: In the *Atzmus*, in the *mashpia*, the *harchava* is very wide

phrases.he: ובקו זה בא כח זה עצמו בבחינת הצמצום שפע והמשכה למקבלים כו'
phrases.en: the *mekablim*: the way it goes, as the line goes down it's narrower and narrower

phrases.he: ואם כן גם בבחינת צמצום והתפשטות שבו, משם הוא בא דווקא
phrases.en: So the *inyan* of the *tzimtzum* and *hispashtus* in the *Kav* comes from the *tzimtzum* and *hispashtus* before, in the *Atzmus*

phrases.he: ודי למבין:

blocks.text: a line, compared to a surface, is a *hiyuli*. In the *Atzmus*, in the *mashpia*, the breadth is very wide. For the *mekablim*, as the line goes down it is narrower and narrower. When you teach college students, you give them much more of a surface than you give to little kids. And that surface too has the *Kav* as its *hiyuli*. But in the *Atzmus* it is in the widest extent: there the breadth is totally wide. and in this *Kav* this very power comes in the form of the *tzimtzum*, drawn down to the receivers.

the contraction and the spreading forth in it also come *davka* from there: the contraction and the spreading forth in the *Kav* come from the contraction and spreading forth before, in the *Atzmus*. Even all the way down here, where there is a total *tzimtzum* and a tiny, tiny little light, this is *mamash* the power of the *Aibershter* Himself. What does it mean exactly, "from there"? The power that is down here is *mamash* the power from there. Even in a kindergarten, you are still getting the whole power of the teacher.

reviewQuestions.question: Why does the *Kav* come as a mere line, if it has in it the power of the first light *mamash* as the *Ein Sof*?
How do the long *nun* and the *ish tevuna* show that the lower the light goes, the higher it shows?
What are the two opposite powers in the *Kav*, and how does the prisoner who goes from the guard to the judge to the king show that they depend on each other?
Why is it a mistake to think of the *reshimu* and the *Kav* as things, and what are they really talking about?
Where does a light beyond the *kav hamida*, or a light held back, come from? Use the trip to NASA and the class that has to sit and do nothing.
Why are the *chesed* and *gevura* of the Essence called by opposite names in this parenthesis, and what does the seal in the wax have to do with it?
